segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: "I named him primary anyway — the domestic history, the breakup timing, the locked door, that's a pattern worth acting on"
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The detective designates the ex as a working theory before forensic results, with a documented plausible resource-allocation rationale and no hidden target bias assigned to this segment.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: "We walk in already knowing the swab didn't match him"; "once my partner made the case ... the DNA on its own didn't feel like it outweighed that"; "nobody was formally assigned to run down the loitering report"
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Groupthink target: the team converges on retaining the ex as primary despite the known negative DNA result, and the dissenting rear-entrance lead receives no independent follow-up.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: "Second witness closes the two-hour gap completely"; "I kept coming back to the fact that it wasn't enough to undo what we'd already built around him"
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Cognitive dissonance target: the closed alibi and detailed alternative description are framed as insufficient to override the already-committed ex theory, with the known negative DNA treated as non-dispositive.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: "that statement got the most space and read as the strongest piece on the page"; "it was also just the last substantial thing that had come in"
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Recency Effects target: the newest detailed witness statement receives disproportionate prominence in the referral memo partly because it was fresh in memory rather than because of a complete comparative evidence review.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The location, mechanism, reasoning operation, and quote are correct, but anchoring bias is not the hidden target label Cognitive dissonance and is not an approved alias.

The candidate is correctly localized and related to the hidden group decision, but it is explicitly hedged and does not establish full convergence on the basis of social pressure or full suppression of dissent.

candidates.details: The candidate identifies the correct briefing episode and a plausible social-influence interpretation, but the raw interview also supports ordinary team convergence and a substantive evidence-based rationale. The candidate therefore falls short of the hidden Groupthink mechanism.

high_only.detection_interpretation: Only the high-confidence recency finding is detected; the groupthink and cognitive-dissonance segments are missed.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: The moderate anchoring finding adds a detection at the cognitive-dissonance segment, while the groupthink segment remains missed because only a candidate was produced.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: No low-confidence identified findings are present, so this threshold equals high_and_moderate.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: Including candidates recovers all positive segments, but the added candidate remains an instance-level false positive rather than a true positive.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: Full mechanism overlap at the day-three evidence-reconciliation episode, but the benchmark target label is Cognitive dissonance.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: obs_001 claims one retrieved paper and provides citation metadata, but the actual retrieved passage and retrieval logs were not supplied. obs_002 explicitly discloses no retrieved support. No corpus-fidelity score is calculated.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Segment F1 rises from 0.5000 to 0.8000 and mechanism-first instance F1 rises from 0.5000 to 0.8000; strict instance F1 falls from 0.5000 to 0.4000 because the moderate anchoring finding is a strict false positive.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: No change: there are no low-confidence identified findings.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: Segment F1 rises to 1.0000, while strict instance F1 falls to 0.3333 and mechanism-first instance F1 falls to 0.6667 because the candidate is an instance-level false positive.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the RAG detects 2 of 3 positive segments with no segment false alarms (hit rate 0.6667; F1 0.8000).
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, strict instance scoring yields 1 true positive, 2 false negatives, and 1 false positive (precision 0.5000; recall 0.3333; F1 0.4000).
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, mechanism-first scoring yields 2 true positives, 1 false negative, and no false positives (precision 1.0000; recall 0.6667; F1 0.8000).
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidate recovers the missed groupthink segment at the segment level but does not meet full instance-level mechanism requirements, so it adds no true positive and adds an instance-level false positive at the fourth threshold.
main_failure_modes: The RAG labels the cognitive-dissonance instance as anchoring bias, creating a strict taxonomy error despite full mechanism overlap.
The RAG does not identify Groupthink as an occurrence; its conformity candidate remains too hedged and incomplete.
The claimed retrieved citation cannot be fidelity-checked without retrieved material or logs.
main_strengths: The recency-effect instance is an exact label, location, mechanism, and evidence match at high confidence.
Both identified findings use valid, directly supportive interview quotations.
The RAG avoids falsely classifying the neutral initial-theory segment.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run has strong segment localization and good mechanism coverage once moderate confidence is included, but weaker strict taxonomy performance. Candidate inclusion improves segment recall while worsening instance-level precision because the groupthink candidate is a near miss rather than a full match.
